rows.answer: Mutual funds may avail intraday borrowing for all unitholder pay‑outs such as redemptions, IDCW pay‑outs, interest etc.; for pay‑ins with respect to investments made by the scheme; for mark‑to‑market obligations and foreign‑exchange settlements; for repayment of existing borrowings; and, additionally, solely for meeting redemption and other pay‑outs to unitholders as specified under Regulation 42(1) of the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026. [1][2][4]
The intraday borrowing conditions in the July 10 2026 circular become effective on 1 September 2026[2][4].
The cost of intraday borrowing is borne by the Asset Management Company (AMC) [1][5].

The Master Circular (2026) requires that any borrowing exceeding 10% of a scheme’s net assets be disclosed, but it does not set a specific ceiling at 20% or prohibit borrowing beyond that level [1]. Therefore, while borrowing more than 20% is not expressly forbidden in the cited documents, such borrowing would have to be disclosed because it exceeds the 10% threshold [1].
The risk‑ometer for mutual fund schemes shows six risk levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High[5][2].
A Large Cap Fund must invest at least 80% of its total assets in large‑cap stocks (minimum investment 80% of total assets) [2][3].
An open‑ended scheme must have at least 20 investors, and no single investor may hold more than 25% of the scheme’s corpus[1][2][3][4][5].
The certification examination for mutual fund distributors is conducted by the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM) [1][2][3][4].

The Master Circular for Mutual Funds identified as HO/24/13/11(1)2026‑IMD‑POD‑1/I/7602/2026 is the master circular presently in force. It became effective on 1 April 2026 and supersedes the earlier Master Circular dated 27 June 2024. [1][1]
The Master Circular for Mutual Funds SEBI/HO/IMD/DF2/CIR/P/2020/156, issued on 24 August 2020 and effective from 24 August 2020, was the applicable master circular in January 2021. [1]

It amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 to permit intraday borrowings by mutual funds for various purposes[1].
